source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Advanced Keyspace Accessor
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the couchbase.* operator family (get/insert/upsert/replace/delete/increment/decrement/touch/mutateIn/lookupIn) exposed to Eventing Function handlers for KV access beyond basic bucket-map syntax; a genuinely new structural primitive family specific to Eventing's JavaScript runtime

concepts.label: Sub-Document MUTATEIN Operation
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - partial-document mutation operator (insert/replace/remove/array ops) available since Couchbase Server 7.6

concepts.label: Sub-Document LOOKUPIN Operation
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - partial-document read operator available since Couchbase Server 7.6.2

concepts.label: Extended Attributes (XATTRs)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - document metadata layer accessible only via explicit opt-in on MUTATEIN/LOOKUPIN operations

concepts.label: Optional cache parameter
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the { "cache": true } third argument enabling a per-node, cross-Function, 1-second RYOW cache on GET operations

concepts.label: Optional self_recursion parameter
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the { "self_recursion": true } argument that lifts default suppression of a Function's own source-bucket mutations, available since Couchbase Server 7.6

concepts.label: Couchbase Server 7.6
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - version badge, consistent with the recurring server-version-string-citation pattern flagged in prior rounds

relations.subject: eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor
relations.evidence: Advanced Keyspace Accessors use the same bucket bindings defined in the handler as [Basic Keyspace Accessors](eventing-language-constructs.md#bucket%5Faccessors), but they expose a larger set of options and operators.

relations.subject: eventing:mutatein-operation
relations.evidence:
Couchbase Server 7.6

`result = couchbase.mutateIn(binding, meta, subdoc_operation_array, options)`

relations.subject: eventing:lookupin-operation
relations.evidence:
Couchbase Server 7.6.2

`result = couchbase.lookupIn(binding, meta, subdoc_array, options)`

relations.subject: eventing:self-recursion-parameter
relations.evidence:
Couchbase Server 7.6

You can use the optional fourth parameter `{ "self_recursion": true }` to prevent the suppression of recursive source bucket mutations and to process the mutations that you have just created.

relations.subject: eventing:mutatein-operation
relations.evidence: By default, a MUTATEIN operation does not modify Extended Attributes (XATTRs). To modify a document's XATTRs, you must: Pass `xattrs` as the third argument of your OnUpdate function.

relations.subject: eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor
relations.evidence: For the Advanced GET operation, the binding can have an access level of read or read/write. For all other operations, the binding must have an access level of read/write.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: You can use the wildcard `*` in an Eventing Function's scope or collection to listen to multiple collections.

relations.subject: eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor
relations.evidence: If the binding used by the Advanced Keyspace Accessor also contains a wildcard `*` for its scope or collection, you must use the additional `meta.keyspace` parameter.

relations.subject: eventing:meta-keyspace-parameter
relations.evidence: meta.keyspace | Object | The keyspace of the document to be used for the operation. Must be in the JavaScript format "keyspace": { "bucket\_name": string, "scope\_name": string, "collection\_name": string }.

relations.subject: eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor
relations.evidence: [Advanced Accessor Handler scriptlets](eventing-examples.md#examples-scriptlets-advanced-accessors) for complete examples of Advanced Keyspace Accessors, including JavaScript, input mutations, output mutations, and log messages

notable_absence.finding: No privilege, capella-role, or credential type gates any Advanced Keyspace Accessor operation on this page; the only access-control-shaped constraint found is binding access level (read vs. read/write), which is a Function-configuration setting rather than a Capella RBAC construct.

cross_component_finding: The meta.keyspace parameter is the clearest evidence in this batch that Eventing's wildcard-listening model is built directly on the bucket/scope/collection triple established elsewhere in the registry ('Must be in the JavaScript format "keyspace": { "bucket_name": string, "scope_name": string, "collection_name": string }') - Eventing did not invent its own addressing scheme for multi-collection functions, it reused the existing keyspace shape verbatim as a JS object.
